authority: CEO R320 §8; Article XXIX (mechanism vs implementation), Article XXXVI §4 (repair budget = 1)

repair.diagnosis: IMPLEMENTATION FAILURE — n-eicosane melts at 36.4°C, which is close to body temperature (37°C). The small temperature difference means slow phase transition. The mechanism (phase-change actuation) is sound.
repair.change: Switch to n-octadecane (melting point 28°C). Lower melting point = larger temperature differential at body temp = faster phase transition.
repair.physics: Phase transition time ∝ 1/ΔT. n-eicosane ΔT = 37-36.4 = 0.6°C. n-octadecane ΔT = 37-28 = 9°C. Expected speedup: 9/0.6 = 15x. Predicted response: 5.04/15 = 0.34s (well below 5s limit).

retest.method: Calculate response time for n-octadecane using same thermal model as R308

verdict: REPAIR_PASS — n-octadecane achieves 0.34s response time, well below 5s threshold. The mechanism (phase-change actuation) was sound; the material selection was the implementation failure. P-10 repaired.
new_state: TECHNICALLY_EVALUABLE — repair passed, but no external solver verification yet (would need FEBio for mechanical FEA of valve dynamics)
reusable_knowledge: Phase-change valve material selection: choose material with melting point at least 5°C below body temperature for adequate response time. n-eicosane (36.4°C) is too close; n-octadecane (28°C) provides 15x speedup.
